title: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)

sections.label: Rules-based order unravelling
sections.summary: The motion reduces Head U by $100, noting that the rules-based international order is unravelling and protectionism will disproportionately affect Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Mr Chair, I move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head U of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Sir, the rules-based international order that has prevailed for decades – characterised by free trade, global supply chains and the development of multilateral institutions, like the United Nations (UN) and the World Health Organization (WHO), and international law and treaties like the Paris Agreement on climate change – is being unravelled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Countries have adopted more protectionist measures, like tariffs and restrictions on trade, contributing to the fragmentation of global supply chains and economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As a small and open country, these trends will disproportionately affect us in Singapore.

sections.label: Public Service consultation preparation
sections.summary: It asks how the Public Service is preparing officers for a changing domestic landscape needing engagement and a fracturing world order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, greater consultation requires not just a willingness to consult, but the dedication and commitment to put in the time and effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, in light of this, how is the Public Service preparing our officers to better understand and meet the challenges posed by a changing domestic landscape, where there is a greater need of engagement and consultation, as well as a fracturing world order?

sections.label: GRIT@Gov traineeship programme
sections.summary: It describes the GRIT@Gov traineeship launched in October 2025 and asks how awareness, matching and role clarity can be strengthened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, as we speak about transformation across the Singapore economy, it is also equally important to understand the transformation within the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am going to talk about the launch of the GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) programme, or the GRIT@Gov, which reflects an important move to attract young Singaporeans to develop them for meaningful careers within Public Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And this is also to help the much-needed experience that they will then be able to better compete in the market as experience is a prerequisite to many jobs and of course, to get better pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, recent news reporting indicates that placements are still building up since the programme started in October 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We want to understand how can awareness, matching and role clarity be better strengthened, so that suitable candidates are able to see GRIT@Gov not just as a traineeship but as a credible entry pathway into long-term Public Service careers?

sections.label: Workplace grievance resolution principles
sections.summary: It asks how the Government will apply early resolution and mediation principles to promote fair handling of workplace grievances in the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the Act does not apply directly to Public Officers, the underlying principles remain relevant within the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We hope to understand in this context; how will the Government apply the principles of early resolution and mediation that will be reinforced to promote fair and timely handling of workplace grievances?

sections.label: Overseas postings and exchanges
sections.summary: It states that overseas postings, exchanges, attachments to international organisations and stints in private and people sectors are being ramped up.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To help public officers build up their global exposure and connections, we are ramping up overseas postings and exchanges, attachments to international organisations and stints in the private and people sectors.

sections.label: Partnership proposals and digital transactions
sections.summary: It states that in 2025 agencies received over 1,600 partnership proposals and that 99% of government-to-citizen transactions can be completed digitally.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In 2025, agencies received over 1,600 partnership proposals from citizens, corporates, community groups and organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Today, 99% of government-to-citizen transactions, like Community Development Council (CDC) vouchers, can be completed digitally.

sections.label: Officers in foundational programme
sections.summary: More than 4,300 officers from over 69 public agencies have completed the movement's foundational programme to date.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To date, more than 4,300 officers from over 69 public agencies have gone through the foundational programme under the movement.

sections.label: Ministerial discretion under law
sections.summary: The law gives Ministers and officials discretion to judge each case on its facts, with Cabinet discussing the most important issues.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The law confers discretion on Ministers and other officials so that they can exercise their judgement on how best to deal with each case based on the facts, instead of mechanically applying a rigid rule.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The rationale for a discretionary function, its scope and limits, and any applicable safeguards, would have been debated by this House when the legislation was passed.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Each Minister is responsible for exercising the statutory functions assigned to him or her.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The most important issues are referred to and discussed by Cabinet before a final decision is taken.

sections.label: RIE2030 funding commitment
sections.summary: The Government's $37 billion commitment under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2030 Plan reflects foresight and discipline.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government’s $37 billion commitment under Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2030 (RIE2030) Plan reflects foresight and discipline.

sections.label: Anchoring value and tracking impact
sections.summary: Anchoring value means retaining IP, scaling Singapore-headquartered enterprises and creating high value roles, with sharper tracking of economic impact.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Anchoring value means retaining intellectual property (IP), scaling Singapore-headquartered enterprises and creating high value roles for Singaporeans across the innovation chain.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But as investment scales up, it is appropriate that we continue sharpening how we track economic impact.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This includes attention to IP anchored locally, enterprise growth driven by domestic innovation, productivity gains linked to publicly funded research as well as high-skilled opportunities created for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Stewarding RIE2030 investment
sections.summary: With disciplined stewardship, anchoring value and renewing talent, RIE2030 will focus on the economy, national priorities and globally competitive research capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If we steward this investment with discipline, anchoring value and renewing talent, Singapore will not merely participate in technological change.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would welcome the Minister’s thoughts on how RIE2030 will continue strengthening value capture and structured renewal pathways as we move into this next phase.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: RIE2030 will focus on contributing to our economy and national priorities, and ensuring our research capabilities and talent remain globally competitive.

sections.label: Semiconductor RIE Flagship
sections.summary: The Semiconductor RIE Flagship seeks to strengthen Singapore's position in the global semiconductor supply chain and advance chip and equipment manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, the Semiconductor RIE Flagship seeks to strengthen Singapore's position as a strategic node in the global semiconductor supply chain, building new research capabilities and advancing the manufacturing of chips and semiconductor equipment in Singapore.

sections.label: R&D associated jobs 2023
sections.summary: In 2023, more than 60,000 jobs were associated with R&D activities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In 2023, more than 60,000 jobs were associated with R&D activities.

sections.label: NRF Postdoctoral Award
sections.summary: NRF has introduced a new Postdoctoral Award to support high potential postdoctoral talents to pursue independent research.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: NRF has introduced a new Postdoctoral Award to support high potential postdoctoral talents to pursue independent research.

sections.label: Singapore 2035 NDC emissions target
sections.summary: Singapore's 2035 NDCs aim to reduce emissions to 45 to 50 million tonnes of carbon dioxide, supporting the 2050 net-zero goal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Singapore's 2035 Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) aim to reduce emissions to 45 to 50 million tonnes of carbon dioxide supporting our 2050 net-zero goal.

sections.label: Carbon tax and 2030 NDC
sections.summary: The question asks about progress on domestic mitigation measures to meet the 2030 NDC target, given the Prime Minister's mention of possibly adopting the lower carbon tax range.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Second, in view of the Prime Minister's mention during Budget on Carbon Tax pricing to possibly adopt the lower range of $50 per million tonne of carbon dioxide, I would like to ask what is the progress on Singapore's key domestic mitigation measures to meet our 2030 NDC target?

sections.label: Prime Minister carbon tax range
sections.summary: The Prime Minister signalled in his Budget speech that the Government is considering the lower end of the planned carbon tax range for 2030, citing weaker global climate momentum.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Prime Minister signalled in his Budget speech that the Government is considering the lower end of the planned carbon tax range for 2030, citing weaker global climate momentum.

sections.label: Carbon credits and electricity imports
sections.summary: The question asks whether constrained supply of high-quality international carbon credits has pushed Singapore towards higher reliance on low carbon electricity import projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Has the constrained supply of high-quality international carbon credits pushed Singapore towards higher reliance on low carbon electricity import projects?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: These are pertinent questions as our electricity use accelerates, particularly with the expansion of data centre capacity.

sections.label: Carbon tax alignment with trading partners
sections.summary: Business community thanks Government's pragmatic carbon tax trajectory and asks how alignment with major trading partners is assessed to minimise carbon leakage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The business community thanks the Government's position that our carbon tax trajectory is set with a pragmatic and calibrated approach – taking into account international developments, development competitiveness and the progress of decarbonisation technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How does Government continuously assess whether Singapore's carbon pricing remains aligned with major trading partners to minimise carbon leakage and unintended relocation of emissive activities?

sections.label: Budget 2026 carbon tax range
sections.summary: The Prime Minister acknowledged declining global climate momentum, which may see Singapore pegging its carbon tax at the lower end of $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In his Budget 2026 speech, the Prime Minister acknowledged the decline in global climate momentum, which may see Singapore pegging its carbon tax at the lower end of the $50 to $80 per tonne range by 2030.

sections.label: Expected carbon tax rates
sections.summary: The passage asks what the expected carbon tax rates are, considering all known factors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What is the expected carbon tax rates, considering all known factors?

sections.label: Climate impacts and regressive policy
sections.summary: 2024 was one of the warmest years on record with rainfall 8.1% above average, and regressive policy surged over 500% in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Its impact is already felt. 2024 was one of the warmest years on record, with total rainfall 8.1% above the long-term annual average.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A report by Climate Forecasting Consortium's Inevitable Policy Response showed that decelerating or regressive policy surged by over 500% in 2025.

sections.label: Green Skills Report findings
sections.summary: The Green Skills Report defines green jobs and skills, finding such competencies integrated into mainstream roles, with about 5,000 workers projected needed by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The recently published Green Skills Report defines what are green jobs and green skills, finding that such competencies are being integrated into mainstream roles, not just specialist jobs, with about 5,000 workers projected to be needed by 2030.

sections.label: Transferable skills and NCCS coordination
sections.summary: The passage lists transferable skills and suggests NCCS consider a coordination function to map sector exposure, identify skills and align industries, agencies and employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These are transferable skills to electric vessel servicing, offshore renewables support, battery systems and industrial energy efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I suggest the National Climate Change Secretariat (NCCS) considers establishing a coordination function to map sector exposure, identify transferable skills and align industries, agencies and employers early.

sections.label: China emissions reduction commitment
sections.summary: China, the world's largest emitter, has committed for the first time to absolute emissions reductions beyond its peak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: China, the world's largest emitter, has committed for the first time to absolute emissions reductions beyond its peak.

sections.label: Carbon tax increase
sections.summary: The carbon tax has been increased to $45 per tonne this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As we announced earlier, we have increased the carbon tax to $45 per tonne this year.

sections.label: Carbon pricing adoption expansion
sections.summary: Carbon pricing adoption is expanding, driven partly by the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, with Thailand, Malaysia and Japan taking measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Carbon pricing adoption continues to expand, driven in part by measures such as the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, which started this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In our region, Thailand introduced a carbon tax last year, Malaysia plans to do so this year and Japan will make its national emissions trading system mandatory this year.

sections.label: Reviewing carbon tax trajectory
sections.summary: The carbon tax trajectory for 2028 and beyond is under review, with future rates announced in advance and possible positioning toward $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As Mr Mark Lee and Ms Lee Hui Ying have noted, we must manage the near- to medium-term cost impact on our households and businesses, relative to our regional competitors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are therefore reviewing the carbon tax trajectory for 2028 and beyond, and will announce future rates in advance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: If the global push for climate action slows down significantly, we may need to position ourselves toward the lower end of the previously announced range of $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

sections.label: Solar deployment target reached
sections.summary: The 2030 solar deployment target of two gigawatt-peak was reached ahead of schedule and will be raised to two gigawatt-peak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: For example, we have reached our 2030 solar deployment target of two gigawatt-peak ahead of schedule and will raise our 2030 target to two gigawatt-peak, as announced by the Prime Minister in his Budget speech earlier.

sections.label: Fifth agreement with Thailand
sections.summary: The fifth agreement will be operationalised on 31 March with Thailand, with a call for projects under the partnership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Building on this momentum, we will operationalise our fifth agreement on 31 March with Thailand, with a call for projects under our partnership.

sections.label: FAST-P green investments funding
sections.summary: Singapore pledged up to US$500 million to FAST-P, and the Green Investments Partnership reached a first close with US$510 million committed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Singapore has pledged up to US$500 million to FAST-P, with the aim of crowding in up to US$5 billion of commercial capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The Green Investments Partnership under FAST-P has achieved its first close with US$510 million in committed capital – 10 times the Government's initial contribution of US$50 million.

sections.label: National Adaptation Plan development
sections.summary: A National Adaptation Plan is being developed to strengthen resilience across infrastructure, public health, water, food and coastal protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We must undertake adaptation as a core pillar of our long-term climate resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are developing a National Adaptation Plan to strengthen resilience across infrastructure, public health, water, food and coastal protection.

sections.label: Global carbon emissions increase
sections.summary: The annual increase in global carbon emissions is now 0.3%, one-fifth of the decade before the Paris Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The annual increase in global carbon emissions is now at 0.3% – one-fifth that in the decade before the Paris Agreement was signed – although this is still not enough to keep global warming below 1.5 degrees Celsius.

sections.label: Regional climate capacity building
sections.summary: Singapore is working with international partners to reach regional contacts, especially in developing countries, to train professionals and build capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: On the regional cooperation, indeed, we are working with international partners to reach out to our regional contacts, especially in the developing countries, to help to train professionals and to help to train skills development to do capacity building, so that we can come together and move forward together in this journey towards climate action.

sections.label: Energy supply security approach
sections.summary: A multi-pronged approach is adopted to ensure energy supply and security in case of blockage or disruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman
sentences.text: As we all know, certain position or a certain situation can happen that this may be blocked or disrupted?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We adopt a multi-pronged approach to ensure our energy supply and security.

sections.label: Energy diversification and fertility rate
sections.summary: Diversification is the key strategy for energy security, and Singapore's resident total fertility rate stands at 0.97.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, we would not be able to rely on any single particular source, any single particular form of energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, I think diversification is our key strategy in ensuring energy security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Chairman, Singapore's latest resident total fertility rate (TFR) stands at 0.97, a historic low.

sections.label: New citizenships versus citizen births
sections.summary: New citizenships granted reached around 23,000 per year, and could exceed citizen births of around 29,000 in 2024 if births keep declining.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: New citizenships granted reached an all-time-high – around 23,000 per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If our citizen births – around 29,000 in 2024 – continue to decline, there will come a day when the number of new citizenships given to immigrants exceeds the number of Singaporean babies born.

sections.label: Wealth Gini at 0.55
sections.summary: Singapore's Wealth Gini stands at 0.55, higher than the Income Gini and likely an underestimate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our Wealth Gini stands at 0.55, higher than our Income Gini and likely an underestimate.

sections.label: Hypothetical $5,000 birth endowment
sections.summary: A hypothetical $5,000 endowment at birth could compound to $200,000, or $400,000 and more with an equities-based strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Potentially structured as an extension of the same scheme, drawing on the same commercial providers, a hypothetical $5,000 endowment at birth, compounded over a lifetime, could become $200,000 with a conservative lifecycle approach, or even $400,000 and more with a more aggressive equities-based strategy.

sections.label: Transnational marriages and pass holders
sections.summary: Transnational marriages rose from 30% to 37% in five years, with about 270,000 Long-Term Visit Pass holders and a stable PR population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The proportion of transnational marriages has risen from 30% to 37% in the last five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Today, more than one in three marriages involves a Singaporean and a non-Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There are approximately 270,000 Long-Term Visit Pass holders, many part of Singaporean family units.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Permanent Resident (PR) population has remained relatively stable at 520,000 to 540,000.

sections.label: Marriages fall, TFR projected
sections.summary: Singapore's marriages fell 6.2% in 2025 compared to 2024, projected to worsen the ultra-low TFR of 0.97 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Singapore's marriages fell by 6.2% in 2025 compared to 2024 and this significant drop is projected to worsen Singapore's ultra-low TFR, which stood at 0.97 in 2024.

sections.label: Infertility among couples
sections.summary: SingHealth data shows roughly one in six couples experience infertility in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: SingHealth data shows roughly one in six couples experience infertility here.

sections.label: ART MediSave and co-funding
sections.summary: Higher MediSave limits and Government co-funding for ART at private clinics, expanding withdrawals to six cycles and covering egg freezing and screenings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Three, higher MediSave utilisation limits for ART, allowing treatments in private clinics to reduce long public hospital waits where time is critical.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And four, Government co-funding for ART at private clinics, expanding MediSave withdrawals from three to six cycles, coverage for elective egg freezing, subsidised couple screenings and enhanced workplace support for fertility and family building.

sections.label: Working mother tax incentives
sections.summary: Calls for reinstating working mother tax incentives so mothers who increase earnings claim larger relief per child.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We must also continue to support continuous career progression for working parents, especially mothers, to ensure stable incomes amid rising costs for children and ageing parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I urge reinstating working mother tax incentives, allowing mothers who increase their earnings to claim larger relief per child.

sections.label: Singapore TFR 0.97
sections.summary: Singapore faces a similar precipice today with a TFR of 0.97.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Today, with a TFR of 0.97, Singapore faces a similar precipice.

sections.label: Smaller birth cohorts workforce
sections.summary: Smaller birth cohorts entering the workforce mean topping up the resident workforce with more new citizens and PRs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: This shift 25 years ago is now creating a moment of reckoning for the size of our resident workforce today, because these smaller birth cohorts are now starting to enter the workforce 25 years later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: So, for the first time in Singapore, the birth cohorts hitting working age are smaller than the cohorts aged 65 to 69, that is, those reaching retirement and re-employment age roughly – smaller by 30,000 persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The stark implication is this – to keep our resident workforce growing at the same modest rate as in previous years, we will have to top-up our resident workforce with more new citizens and PRs by around the same number over five years.

sections.label: NS for new male citizens
sections.summary: Proposes introducing National Service for new male citizens of working age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: First, introduce National Service (NS) for new male citizens of working age.

sections.label: Flexi-care leave scheme
sections.summary: Urges a flexi-care leave scheme so workers can respond to caregiving needs without choosing between jobs and families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: The Prime Minister has sent a clear signal that support for our young parents is important.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: I urge the Minister to consider a flexi-care leave scheme, which is already adopted by some private organisations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: This will give workers the assurance and flexibility to respond to caregiving needs across different life stages without having to choose between their jobs and their families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: It can be for accompanying parents to medical appointments, caring for a child who is unwell or attending to urgent caregiving needs at home – or simply a day to recharge for their own mental well-being, no questions asked.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: This is not just a matter of compassion, but of workforce sustainability.

sections.label: Parental leave takes effect
sections.summary: Thirty weeks of parental leave takes full effect this April.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thirty weeks of parental leave takes full effect this April.

sections.label: Marriage and Parenthood survey
sections.summary: In the Government's 2021 Marriage and Parenthood survey, 92% of married Singaporeans said they wanted two or more children.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the Government's 2021 Marriage and Parenthood survey, 92% of married Singaporeans said they wanted two or more children.

sections.label: Made For Families certification
sections.summary: The speaker asks to pilot a Made For Families workplace certification, a tiered national standard measuring where workplaces support family life.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Good intentions, every one of them, but no single standard that tells an employer or a jobseeker what a family-friendly workplace actually looks like.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I have one ask – pilot a Made For Families workplace certification, a tiered national standard that measures where the workplace truly supports family life.

sections.label: Shared Parental Leave funding
sections.summary: The Government has committed approximately $400 million annually for Shared Parental Leave at steady state.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government has committed approximately $400 million annually for Shared Parental Leave at steady state.

sections.label: TFR and median age
sections.summary: Singapore's TFR remains around 0.97 and its median age exceeds 42.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: Our TFR remains around 0.97, our median age exceeds 42.

sections.label: Employment support measures considered
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government will consider sector-based manpower pools, re-entry support, fractional employment frameworks and job redesign support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: Will the Government consider: (a) Sector-based manpower pools to help firms manage parental leave coverage; (b) Structured re-entry and transitional support for employees returning from extended caregiving; (c) Clearer frameworks and tripartite guidance for fractional and part-time employment models; and (d) Calibrated support for job redesign to make senior employment more productive and less administratively complex?

sections.label: Enhanced Budget support for FWA
sections.summary: Calls for enhanced Budget support including grants, backfilling support and advisory teams to help companies implement flexible work arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I therefore call for enhanced Budget support to help companies undertake meaningful job redesign for win-win FWA implementations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: This should include stronger grants for human resources (HR) transformation, support for temporary backfilling and sector-based advisory teams to guide practical redesign.

sections.label: Extended hours childcare and TFR
sections.summary: Calls for resources to expand extended hours and weekend childcare, noting Singapore's TFR fell below one in 2023 and stayed at 0.97 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Through consultations with unions and our female workers, especially shift workers, we consistently hear that standard childcare hours do not match real work schedules.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I therefore call for more resources to restart and expand extended hours and weekend childcare, particularly in estates with higher concentrations of shift workers, with manpower and wage support to ensure sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Chairman, Singapore's TFR fell below one in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The year 2024 was the Year of the Dragon, which typically gives us a boost in the yearly TFR rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: However, the Dragon could only hold the fort for us by keeping the number steady at 0.97 in 2024.

sections.label: Caregivers' ages and qualifications
sections.summary: States that three in four such caregivers are in their 40s or younger and 66.5% held tertiary qualifications, including degrees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Three in four of such caregivers are in their 40s or younger, and 66.5% held tertiary qualifications, including degrees.

sections.label: SMEs' role in economy
sections.summary: States SMEs form the backbone of Singapore's economy, contributing around 50% of GDP and employing about 70% of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: To create a truly resilient workforce, a mindset shift is especially important amongst SMEs, which form the backbone of Singapore's economy, contributing around 50% of our GDP and employing about 70% of our workforce.

sections.label: Fertility screening subsidies and MediSave
sections.summary: States there are no Government subsidies or MediSave coverage specifically for fertility screening, but means-tested subsidies of up to 70% exist for medically indicated tests at public hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently, there are no Government subsidies or MediSave coverage specifically for fertility screening, but there are means-tested subsidies of up to 70% for fertility tests at public hospitals if such tests are "medically indicated".

sections.label: Subsidies for early fertility screening
sections.summary: Calls for generous subsidies and MediSave coverage for fertility screening within the first year of marriage, at public or private clinics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If they are only undergoing fertility testing for "medical indications", it means that any fertility issues are going to be discovered quite late.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, if we are going to encourage young couples tying the knot to take early steps to undergo fertility screening – such as hormonal profiling and pelvic ultrasounds for women and semen analysis for men – we should extend generous subsidies and allow MediSave coverage to meet the costs if they are carried out within the first year of marriage, for example, whether or not the tests are performed at a public or private clinic.

sections.label: IVF co-funding at public centres
sections.summary: Government co-funds up to 75% of three fresh and three frozen IVF cycles at three public Assisted Reproductive centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Right now, Government co-funding for in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) is for up to 75% for three fresh and three frozen cycles, but only if treatment is sought at our three public Assisted Reproductive centres at Singapore General Hospital (SGH), KK Women's and Children's Hospital (KKH) and National University Hospital (NUH).

sections.label: Extending subsidies to private centres
sections.summary: The strategy to reduce barriers to ART services must include extending subsidies to private Assisted Reproductive centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An essential part of the strategy to reduce barriers to ART services must include the extension of subsidies to cover services provided by private Assisted Reproductive centres.

sections.label: Fertility education and life-course planning
sections.summary: It proposes fertility education at universities, workplaces and premarital programmes, and life-course planning tools, while respecting the choice not to have children.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: First, integrate clear, evidence-based fertility education into existing young adult touchpoints – universities, workplaces and premarital programmes – delivered in a neutral and non-judgemental way.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Second, develop life-course planning tools that help individuals map career and family aspirations in parallel, rather than sequentially.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: In fact, I support the hon Member, Ms Hany Soh's proposal on fertility screening after couples go through ROM.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: If someone does not want children, that choice must be respected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: But if someone hopes to have children "someday", policy should ensure that "someday" is grounded in realistic and informed awareness of biological timelines.

sections.label: Subsidies reduced across IVF cycles
sections.summary: Subsidies currently decrease with successive IVF cycles, though medical evidence shows cumulative live birth chances increase across cycles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Today, couples undergoing assisted reproductive techniques receive subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: However, the current structure reduces subsidies with successive IVF cycles – a model developed when clinical evidence was more limited.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Current medical evidence shows that the cumulative chance of achieving a live birth increases across successive IVF cycles.

sections.label: Public health lens and insurance schemes
sections.summary: It urges PMO and MOH to view fertility as public health and PMO and MAS to consider inclusive insurance risk-sharing schemes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, may I urge PMO and the Ministry of Health to work together and look at fertility from a public health lens, explore a more progressive approach to subsidies and can PMO also work with the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to consider inclusive insurance schemes that could provide risk-sharing mechanisms.

sections.label: KKH study on miscarriage rates
sections.summary: A 2022 KKH study found 15 to 20% of recorded pregnancies ended in miscarriages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: A 2022 KKH study found 15 to 20% of recorded pregnancies ended in miscarriages.

sections.label: Miscarriage leave and support
sections.summary: India and the UK have miscarriage and bereavement leave; Singapore could consider miscarriage recovery leave, counselling referrals and workplace guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: India offers six weeks paid leave after miscarriage and the UK has amended its Employment Rights Bill for bereavement leave after a pregnancy loss before 24 weeks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Singapore could consider a dedicated miscarriage recovery leave entitlement, automatic referral pathways for counselling support, clear workplace guidelines to support employees experiencing pregnancy loss.

sections.label: Childcare leave during preschool
sections.summary: Singapore could consider incremental steps to increase childcare leave during preschool years, especially the first year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Singapore could consider incremental steps increasing childcare leave during preschool years, especially the first year when illness is most frequent.

sections.label: In-home postpartum visits
sections.summary: The speaker proposes enhancing follow-up healthcare after delivery with structured in-home postpartum visits in the first year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While we already have follow-up healthcare after delivery, I propose enhancing this with structured in-home postpartum visits in the first year.

sections.label: Career Comeback Programme incentives
sections.summary: A regional country has a Career Comeback Programme with job databases, coaching and tax incentives; the PMO is asked to explore a similar incentive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A country in the region has instituted a Career Comeback Programme, providing mothers returning to work with job databases, career coaching and a 12-month income tax exemption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Companies hiring returnees may qualify for a 50% tax deduction on the employee's salary for up to 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will the PMO explore a career comeback tax incentive to provide relief for employers who intentionally hire them, signalling that both society and Government support their return?

sections.label: Resident babies welcomed
sections.summary: Last year, around 27,500 resident babies were welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Last year, we welcomed around 27,500 resident babies.

sections.label: Preliminary resident TFR 2025
sections.summary: Preliminary resident TFR for 2025 is 0.87, down from 0.97 the year before and 1.24 a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Our preliminary resident TFR for 2025 is 0.87.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This is a significant drop from the TFR of 0.97 that many of you quoted for the year before, and much lower than the TFR of 1.24 just a decade ago.

sections.label: Citizen population shrinking 2040s
sections.summary: Without new measures, the citizen population will begin to shrink by the early 2040s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: If no new measures are taken, our citizen population will start to shrink by the early part of 2040s.

sections.label: Managing immigration and ethnic balance
sections.summary: The government will maintain the broad ethnic balance of the citizen population and manage immigration pace and impact carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We will maintain the broad ethnic balance of our citizen population and continue to carefully manage the impact of immigration on our population composition to preserve the overall texture of our society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We will carefully manage the pace of immigration and ensure we do not bring in immigrants faster than we can accommodate.

sections.label: Citizenship and PR integration journeys
sections.summary: New citizens aged 16 to 60 go through the Singapore Citizenship Journey, and a piloted PR Journey programme will be scaled up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: All new citizens between the ages of 16 and 60 go through the Singapore Citizenship Journey, so that they understand our history, our norms, our values and build stronger ties with the local community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We also piloted a new Permanent Resident (PR) Journey programme last year to help new PRs settle in and integrate, and we intend to scale it up shortly.

sections.label: Citizen and PR intake numbers
sections.summary: Singapore expects 25,000 to 30,000 new citizens and about 40,000 PRs annually over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: It is critical that we maintain a stable citizen core, hopefully one that is growing modestly over time, to keep our society and our economy dynamic and vibrant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We expect to take in between 25,000 and 30,000 new citizens annually, over the next five years, depending on our demographic trends including our TFR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Our PR population has remained stable over the past few years, at around 540,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We estimate an intake of about 40,000 PRs annually in the next five years, slightly higher than the 35,000 PRs we granted last year.

sections.label: Foreign workforce growth rate
sections.summary: Over the past five years, the foreign workforce grew at an average of 3.3% per annum, mainly from post-COVID-19 construction catch-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In the past five years, our foreign workforce grew at an average of 3.3% per annum, primarily driven by post-COVID-19 catch-up in construction.

sections.label: Raising EP and S Pass salaries
sections.summary: Employment Pass and S Pass qualifying salaries will be increased to keep pace with local wage benchmarks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As announced at Budget, we will increase our Employment Pass and S Pass qualifying salaries to keep pace with local wage benchmarks.

sections.label: SAESL expansion creates technician jobs
sections.summary: SAESL's $242 million expansion and new training academy are expected to create 500 additional local skilled engine technician jobs over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: With a $242 million expansion and a new training academy supporting its growth plans, SAESL expects to create 500 additional jobs for local skilled engine technicians over the next five years.

sections.label: Singaporean PMET job growth
sections.summary: Over 10 years, Singaporeans in PMET jobs rose by 308,000 while Employment and S Pass holders rose by 24,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Overall, in the past 10 years, the number of Singaporeans in professional, managerial, executive and technical (PMET) jobs has increased by 308,000 while the number of Employment and S Pass holders increased by 24,000.

sections.label: Levy, Work Permit and population changes
sections.summary: Levy and Work Permit changes will nudge businesses to hire higher-skilled workers, and total population will grow slower and stay below 6.9 million by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The recent moves to simplify the levy framework, expand sources and raise the maximum age and period of employment for Work Permit Holders, will nudge businesses to hire and retain higher-skilled workers so that they can do more with less manpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Looking ahead, our total population for the next five years will hopefully still grow but most likely at a slower rate than over the past five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And our total population will still be significantly below 6.9 million by 2030, as we have said earlier.

sections.label: Falling TFR existential challenge
sections.summary: Singapore's falling total fertility rate presents a serious and profound existential challenge to society, economy and security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: To conclude, our falling TFR presents a serious and profound existential challenge to our society, our economy and our security.

sections.label: Supporting families and reviewing immigration
sections.summary: Support for Singaporeans to have families must continue, and immigration intake and approach will keep being reviewed to address concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We must never let up in supporting Singaporeans to have families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We will also continue to review our immigration intake and approach, making sure to address the concerns of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Resident TFR fell to 0.87
sections.summary: Preliminary resident TFR for 2025 was 0.87, down from 0.97 in 2024, with resident births falling across all ethnic groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Chairman, as the Deputy Prime Minister indicated earlier, our preliminary resident TFR for 2025 was 0.87, lower than 0.97 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Resident births across all ethnic groups decreased, with the decrease in Chinese births being proportionately larger, at a drop of 15% compared to 2024.

sections.label: Government commitment to reverse decline
sections.summary: The Government says it is wholly committed to addressing the issue and will spare no effort to arrest and reverse the decline.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Government is wholly committed to addressing this issue head on and we will spare no effort to arrest and reverse this decline.

sections.label: France and Paris fertility rates
sections.summary: In 2024, France's TFR was 1.62 while Paris's was 1.27.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2024, France's TFR was 1.62 but Paris's was 1.27.

sections.label: New Workgroup with agencies
sections.summary: A new Workgroup with relevant agencies will be formed to look into these issues holistically and engage widely.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To achieve this, we will form a new Workgroup with the relevant agencies to look into these issues holistically and engage widely across members of the public, businesses and the people sector.

sections.label: Enhanced Marriage and Parenthood Package
sections.summary: Recent years saw an enhanced Marriage and Parenthood Package including Baby Bonus, paternity leave, Shared Parental Leave, Large Families Scheme and Child LifeSG Credits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In recent years, we have significantly enhanced our Marriage and Parenthood Package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These include: (a) the enhanced Baby Bonus Scheme and MediSave Grant for Newborns; (b) doubling paternity leave and making it mandatory; (c) the new 10-week Shared Parental Leave; (d) the Large Families Scheme; and (e) this year, we will provide another $500 of Child LifeSG Credits for every Singaporean child aged 12 and below.

sections.label: Support per child amount
sections.summary: With the addition of the Large Families Scheme, support is up to $54,000 per child.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Today, with the addition of the Large Families Scheme, it is up to $54,000 per child.

sections.label: Budget 2026 subsidy threshold revision
sections.summary: In Budget 2026, the Prime Minister announced income thresholds for preschool and student care subsidies will be revised so more families benefit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In Budget 2026, the Prime Minister announced that the income thresholds for preschool and student care subsidies will be revised so more families can benefit.

sections.label: Median age at first birth
sections.summary: In 2024, the median age of mothers at first birth was around 32 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2024, the median age of mothers at first birth was around 32 years old.

sections.label: Fertility and miscarriage support
sections.summary: Government will raise fertility health awareness, review support for couples, improve workplace support, and study miscarriage support suggestions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To help those with fertility issues we will work with other agencies to raise awareness of fertility health, including improving accessibility of information on existing support, encouraging fertility checks and normalising the seeking of medical attention for fertility issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Those in need can refer to the Made For Families website for current support measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will review the financial and non-financial support couples receive throughout their fertility journeys and work with employers to improve workplace support for employees undergoing fertility treatments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On Ms Valerie Lee's suggestion on support through miscarriages, psychosocial support like counselling is available in public healthcare institutions, but we agree that more can be done and will study her suggestions to see how we can better support those who experienced miscarriages.

sections.label: Education Conversations on arms race
sections.summary: MOE will hold Education Conversations with students, parents, educators, researchers and academics to explore reducing the education arms race.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: MOE will also conduct a series of Education Conversations with students, parents, educators, researchers and academics to explore ways to mitigate the education "arms race", including by reducing the stakes of examinations.

sections.label: Intrusive parents and child outcomes
sections.summary: A 2016 NUS study found children with intrusive parents tended to be overly self-critical and at increased risk of depression and anxiety.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Parents who have high expectations of their children's academic performance may urge them to achieve good grades or over-react when they fall short of expectations, but such actions may cause unintended consequences, as a National University of Singapore study found in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Children with intrusive parents tended to be overly critical of themselves and were at increased risk of developing depression and anxiety symptoms.

sections.label: Employees discouraged from taking leave
sections.summary: Anecdotes persist of employees being subtly discouraged from taking leave or female employees nudged to resign when pregnant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Despite the mandatory leave provisions we have introduced and employment protections, we still hear anecdotes of how some employees are subtly discouraged from taking leave or how female employees are nudged to resign once they are pregnant.

sections.label: Employer family-friendly benefits
sections.summary: Experts attribute higher birth rates to employer-provided family-friendly benefits like hybrid work, onsite baby care, baby bonuses and hampers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Experts attribute the higher birth rates to more family-friendly benefits provided by employers, rather than the Government, to attract and retain the best employees in a competitive environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These include hybrid work arrangements, onsite baby care, baby bonuses and hampers for employees with newborns.

sections.label: Caterpillar Library book circulation
sections.summary: The Caterpillar Library, starting with 100 books, has facilitated circulation of over 10,000 books, connecting neighbours and helping children discover reading.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Starting out with just 100 books, the Caterpillar Library has now facilitated the circulation of over 10,000 books, creating connections between neighbours while helping children discover the joy of reading.

sections.label: Plans for four-pronged approach
sections.summary: In the months ahead, they will work with stakeholders to develop concrete plans for the four-pronged approach laid out earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In the months ahead, we will work with stakeholders to develop concrete plans for the four-pronged approach I laid out earlier.

sections.label: Encouraging younger new citizens
sections.summary: The short answer is yes, they will encourage younger new citizens to come and join them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The short answer is, yes, we will, of course, encourage younger new citizens to come and join us.

sections.label: Timeline and workgroup details
sections.summary: On timeline, they will share details of the workgroup shortly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In terms of timeline, let me put it this way, we will share details of the workgroup shortly.

sections.label: Time is of the essence
sections.summary: The Member is right that time is of the essence; it is an existential issue and they cannot afford to sit back and wait.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Because the Member is right, time is of the essence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It is an existential issue; we cannot afford to sit back and wait.

sections.label: Fresh look at applicants
sections.summary: Because applicants may have assimilated into Singapore society quite well by now, they are keeping all options open and will take a fresh look at many applicants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Because they may have actually assimilated into Singapore society quite well by now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are keeping all options open, so we will take a fresh look at many of these applicants.

sections.label: Maintaining broad social balance
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government will look at a deviation while stressing the importance of maintaining the broad balance of society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I mean, is there a deviation that the Government is prepared to look at in view of the nature of the problem?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But I think it is very important for us to ensure that we maintain the broad balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I am not talking about the decimal digits, but it is important to maintain the balance so that we do not change the overall texture of the society.

sections.label: Rise in digital payments
sections.summary: The speaker agrees digital payments are rising, noting ATM withdrawals fell 13.6% from 2018 to 2024 to $55 billion, a modest decline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Chairman, I agree that there is a clear rise in digital payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, even as ATM withdrawals fell by 13.6% from 2018 to 2024, dropping to $55 billion, the decline was modest.

sections.label: Rivervale Shores two-room flexi-flats
sections.summary: Rivervale Shores has about 1,100 two-room flexi-flats out of 2,500 units, the largest HDB BTO project in Singapore to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The concern is even more salient in the relatively new BTO cluster at Rivervale Shores, where there is a meaningful proportion of two-room flexi-flats, which typically house elderly residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We have close to 1,100 two-room flexi-flats out of a total of 2,500 units for this BTO project, the largest HDB BTO project in Singapore to date.

sections.label: FAST and card payment growth
sections.summary: From 2018 to 2024, FAST payment value rose 511% to $662 billion and credit and debit card payment value rose 52% to $149 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: From 2018 to 2024, the total value of Fast and Secure Transfers (FAST) payments has increased by 511% to $662 billion while the total value of credit and debit card payments have increased by 52% to $149 billion.

sections.label: Cash acceptance and EQDP funding
sections.summary: The speaker seeks mandated cash acceptance for physical merchants and asks about sustained EQDP funding and government-linked listings on the Singapore Exchange.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Under the Currency Act, businesses have the flexibility to determine their accepted payment modes, which must be indicated to customers via a written notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope that the Government would mandate physical merchants to accept cash in payments, in line with other economies such as China and Norway, or at least start with a pilot in existing residential neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In my Adjournment Motion speech earlier this year, I shared that the $5 billion Equity Market Development Programme (EQDP) funding is an important means to encourage more third-party investments into the Singapore equities market, and I hoped it will not be a one-off measure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the S$1.5 billion top-up in Budget 2026 is welcome, ensuring long-term sustainability is key.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Can the Government affirm its commitment to regular, sustained EQDP funding and if so, what are the conditions for determining the amount and timing of funding allocated?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Further, as I have shared last year, while MAS has taken the lead on the demand side, on the supply side, I urge the Government, via its investment entities to similarly take the lead for its companies to list on the Singapore Exchange.

sections.label: Insurance for developmental conditions
sections.summary: MAS and the Life Insurance Association issued 2024 guidance on fair underwriting, but families still report exclusions, higher premiums or rejection.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 2024, MAS and the Life Insurance Association issued guidance on fair underwriting and clearer communication of exclusions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Families still report exclusions, higher premiums or rejection when adults with developmental conditions apply for life or critical illness insurance.

sections.label: Disability insurance rejection data tracking
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will track anonymised disability rejection data and require insurers to justify exclusions or higher premiums.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, will the Government work with MAS and insurers to track anonymised data on disability-related rejections and exclusions, so we have a clearer picture of what is happening?

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Second, when exclusions or higher premiums are applied, will MAS require insurers, if challenged, to show that these decisions are backed by evidence and linked to real risk, as is already required in places like the UK, Australia and parts of the European Union?

sections.label: Cash-lite society goal
sections.summary: The passage states the goal is to build a cash-lite society, not a cashless society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our goal is to build a "cash-lite" society, not a cashless society.

sections.label: DBS ATM at Rivervale Shores
sections.summary: The passage states HDB gave DBS the go-ahead to set up an ATM at Rivervale Shores after a February 13 application.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This is, I believe, the one at Rivervale Shores.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: And on 13 February, DBS submitted an application and I am pleased to inform Mr Chua that HDB has given the go-ahead for DBS to proceed to set up this ATM.

sections.label: MAS monitoring cash acceptance intervention
sections.summary: The passage states MAS is monitoring trends and will assess if intervention, including mandatory cash acceptance by law, is needed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MAS is monitoring the trends and developments in this area and will carefully assess if and when intervention is needed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This includes the possibility of making cash acceptance mandatory by law.

sections.label: EQDP top-up for Singapore equities
sections.summary: The passage states the current EQDP top-up reinforces momentum and enables support for more strategies investing in Singapore equities, including small and mid caps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The current EQDP top-up reinforces the positive momentum and it enables us to support more strategies that invest in Singapore equities including in the small and mid caps.

sections.label: MAS disability insurance complaints review
sections.summary: The passage states MAS received one disability insurance complaint in three years versus eight in 2021-2022, found no unfair underwriting, and will study collecting insurer data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In the past three years, MAS received one complaint relating to insurance coverage for persons with disabilities, compared to a total of eight complaints in 2021 and 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MAS has carefully reviewed all the nine cases and we have not found unfair underwriting practices to date for the nine cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MAS will study Miss Ong's suggestion to collect and monitor relevant data from the insurers.

sections.label: MAS supervisory actions and remarks
sections.summary: MAS will take appropriate supervisory actions against insurers where there are lapses, followed by clarifications on green procurement and an education remark.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Where there are lapses, MAS will take the appropriate supervisory actions against the insurer.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Minister Gan, you have a clarification to make?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I spoke earlier on green procurement and said that the Government has set aside up to 4% of tender evaluation criteria for environmental sustainability considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: Mr Chair, earlier on when I heard Minister Indranee mention that our education and career options should be like an open highway, I could not help but think of a famous song by Jon Bon Jovi, "It's My Life".

sections.label: Withdrawal of cut
sections.summary: The speaker withdraws their cut.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: With that, I would like to withdraw my cut.
